symptom: token credential configuration can cause excessive HELLO traffic on stable connections
diagnostic-action: Measure HELLO rate by connection and inspect token refresh/client version.
qualification: Client-library hypothesis; validate with command telemetry, not cache metrics alone.

symptom: Redis Enterprise database update through PowerShell can return 501
diagnostic-action: Record module/API versions and compare the operation with REST support.
qualification: Management tooling case, not a Redis data-plane failure.

symptom: cache import semantics require explicit destructive-data safeguards
diagnostic-action: Treat import/export as a change operation and require impact review and approval.
qualification: Safety evidence; it does not diagnose runtime performance.

symptom: CLI deletion can reject an access-policy assignment created by the portal
diagnostic-action: Compare assignment resource name/ID and CLI extension/API versions.
qualification: Portal/CLI interoperability case; avoid modifying policy during diagnosis.

symptom: access-policy display may not support GUID assignment names
diagnostic-action: Inspect raw resource IDs and API response rather than relying on display lookup.
qualification: CLI presentation/lookup issue, not proof that authorization is absent.

symptom: Managed Redis access-policy assignment data may be insufficient for diagnosis
diagnostic-action: Collect assignment principal, policy, resource ID and API version from read-only ARM output.
qualification: Management-plane observability gap; redact principal identifiers.

symptom: CLI access-policy lookup can fail for GUID names
diagnostic-action: Use exact resource ID and compare portal, CLI and REST representations.

symptom: retired Redis Enterprise API versions require operator migration
diagnostic-action: Inventory CRD/operator and ARM API versions before diagnosing reconciliation failures.

symptom: module support may lag persistence and Entra-only authentication configuration
diagnostic-action: Compare desired module inputs, rendered ARM model and live resource configuration.
qualification: IaC module capability report; do not infer a platform limitation.

symptom: Managed Redis database name may not be configurable through a module
diagnostic-action: Compare module version, generated resource name and live child-resource ID.
qualification: Bicep module case, not data-plane diagnosis.

symptom: a preview Redis Enterprise API specification omitted an existing SKU
diagnostic-action: Compare requested SKU against ARM API/specification version used by tooling.
qualification: Specific preview API regression; confirm the deployed API version.

symptom: provisioning library API version can lag Redis Enterprise retirement timelines and properties
diagnostic-action: Inventory provisioning SDK and emitted ARM API version.
qualification: Provisioning concern; unrelated to live command latency unless deployment drift exists.
